target: Por más que intenté convencerla, no cambió de opinión.
english: No matter how much I tried to convince her, she didn't change her mind.
tip: 'Intenté' stays indicative: the trying really happened. Por más que + real past fact = indicative; save the subjunctive for trying that is still hypothetical.

target: A pesar de las dificultades, sacamos adelante a la familia.
english: Despite the difficulties, we kept the family afloat.
tip: Sacar adelante unpacks neatly: sacar (pull out) + adelante (forward) – you haul the family forward through the hardship. Spanish speakers use it for kids, businesses, and projects alike.

target: El proyecto fue aprobado por el director.
english: The project was approved by the director.
tip: Passive with ser: "Fue escrito por Cervantes" = It was written by Cervantes. Ser + participle + por (agent). Less common than passive se.

target: Sigue lloviendo desde esta mañana.
english: It's been raining since this morning.
tip: 'Seguir + gerund' = to keep/continue doing. 'Sigue lloviendo' = It keeps raining.

target: Acabo de enterarme de la noticia.
english: I just found out about the news.
tip: 'Acabo de' is present tense but means the past: acabar de + infinitive = just did. 'Acabo de enterarme' = I JUST found out – literally 'I finish of finding out'.

target: Mi padre preguntó qué hora era.
english: My father asked what time it was.
tip: Reported question with "qué." "¿Qué hora es?" → "qué hora era."

target: En cuanto aterricemos, pasaremos por inmigración.
english: As soon as we land, we'll go through immigration.
tip: English says 'as soon as we land' in plain present; Spanish flags it as not-yet-real: 'en cuanto aterricemos' takes subjunctive because the landing hasn't happened.

target: Se puso a llorar cuando recibió la noticia.
english: She started to cry when she received the news.
tip: Ponerse a + infinitive = to suddenly start doing something.

target: Volvió a llamarme a las diez de la noche.
english: He called me again at ten at night.
tip: No word for 'again' here: volver (to return) + a + infinitive = do it again. 'Volvió a llamarme' = literally 'he returned to calling me' = he called again.

target: Serán las tres de la tarde, más o menos.
english: It must be around three in the afternoon.
tip: 'Serán' is future tense used for probability – conjecture about the present.

target: No dejo de pensar en lo que me dijiste.
english: I can't stop thinking about what you told me.
tip: Dejar means 'leave', so 'no dejo de pensar' is literally 'I don't leave off thinking' – the set way to say 'I can't stop thinking'. No word for 'can' needed.

target: De haber sabido que vendríais, habría preparado más comida.
english: Had I known you were coming, I would have prepared more food.
tip: 'De haber sabido' squeezes a whole if-clause into an infinitive: de + haber + participle = 'had I known'. Elegant shortcut for 'si hubiera sabido'.

target: Llevo tres años viviendo en Madrid.
english: I've been living in Madrid for three years.
tip: English needs 'I have been living'; Spanish just carries the time: llevar + time + gerund. 'Llevo tres años viviendo' = literally 'I carry three years living'.

target: Anda buscando trabajo desde que lo despidieron.
english: He's been looking for a job since they fired him.
tip: Andar + gerund = to go around doing something (habitual/ongoing).

target: No bien hubo terminado de hablar, estalló un aplauso.
english: No sooner had he finished speaking than applause broke out.
tip: Hubo + participle = pretérito anterior, very formal/literary.

target: El guía mencionó que el museo cerraba a las cinco.
english: The guide mentioned that the museum closed at five.
tip: Reported speech: "cierra" → "cerraba" (present → imperfect) after "mencionó que."

target: Si bien el informe es completo, falta el análisis financiero.
english: Although the report is complete, the financial analysis is missing.
tip: Si bien: formal concessive connector = although.

target: Acabo de llegar.
english: I just arrived.
tip: A past event in present tense? "Acabo de llegar" is literally "I finish of arriving" – acabar de + infinitive is how Spanish says "just did" without any past tense.

target: Llevo trabajando aquí desde hace cinco años.
english: I've been working here for five years.
tip: "Llevo trabajando" is literally "I carry working" – Spanish carries a duration into the present, so five years of work needs no "have been," just llevar + gerund.

target: No dejes de practicar o perderás lo aprendido.
english: Don't stop practicing or you'll lose what you've learned.
tip: "No dejes de practicar": dejar means "to leave," so Spanish stops actions by leaving them – and the negative works as friendly insistence: be sure to keep practicing.

target: Cuando lleguemos al aeropuerto, te enviaré un mensaje.
english: When we arrive at the airport, I'll send you a message.
tip: "Cuando" + subjunctive for future events.

target: El camarero preguntó si queríamos postre.
english: The waiter asked if we wanted dessert.
tip: Reported question with "si": "¿Quieren postre?" → "si queríamos postre."

target: Por mucho que planifiques, siempre surgirá algo inesperado.
english: No matter how much you plan, something unexpected will always come up.
tip: Why "planifiques," not planificas? "Por mucho que" concedes any imaginable amount of planning – and unreal, open-ended amounts take the subjunctive.

target: La vecina aseguró que había oído un ruido extraño.
english: The neighbor assured us she had heard a strange noise.
tip: Reported speech: "he oído" → "había oído" (present perfect → pluperfect).

target: El mecánico aseguró que el coche estaría listo el viernes.
english: The mechanic assured us the car would be ready on Friday.
tip: Reported speech: "estará" → "estaría" (future → conditional) after "aseguró que."

target: Habia gato encerrado con la oferta del hotel tan barato.
english: There was something fishy about the hotel's offer being so cheap.
tip: "Gato encerrado" – a locked-up cat? Old Spanish purses were cat-skin "gatos" kept hidden in clothing, so a shut-in cat means hidden money: a catch you can't see.

target: Me dijo que aquella había sido la mejor decisión de su vida.
english: She told me that had been the best decision of her life.
tip: 'Esa/esta' becomes 'aquella' in reported speech (distal demonstrative).

target: Ella se puso a llorar de repente.
english: She suddenly started crying.
tip: "Se puso a llorar" – she literally "put herself to" crying. Ponerse a + infinitive marks bursting into an action suddenly, more abrupt than plain empezar.

target: Me arrepiento de no haber ido.
english: I regret not having gone.
tip: Spanish doesn't just regret – it 'repents itself': arrepentirse is always reflexive and needs de. Me arrepiento de no haber ido = I repent-myself of not having gone.

target: El jardín está más bonito que el año pasado.
english: The garden looks nicer than last year.
tip: Why está, not es? Estar flags a change you can see: el jardín está más bonito = it's looking nicer than last year. Es bonito would just state its permanent character.
